title: Helpers of Allah
hookLine: be helpers of Allah, as the disciples of Isa said, we are Allah's helpers (61:14)

cards: Somebody stands at the front of a room and asks: who'll help? There's a pause. People look at their shoes, or their phones.
Then one hand goes up, then another, and suddenly there's a team. A lot of charity drives and community kitchens start in that pause.
The last verse of Surah As-Saff goes back to one of those moments, long before Medina, and to a teacher the Qur'an calls Isa son of Maryam, the man Christians know as Jesus.

teach.b: Verse fourteen. Pickthall: "O ye who believe! Be Allah's helpers, even as Jesus son of Mary said unto the disciples: Who are my helpers for Allah? They said: We are Allah's helpers."
The word for helpers is ansar, the same word that later named the people of Medina who took in the Prophet ﷺ and the emigrants, the people of the lamp put out a week ago.
The word for disciples is hawariyyun, and commentators explained it differently.
Some said it came from washing and whitening cloth, because some were fullers; others pointed to the purity of their hearts, or said it simply meant close supporters.

teach.h: WHO ARE MY HELPERS FOR GOD?
teach.b: The same scene appears in Surah Al 'Imran: Isa senses denial among his people, asks who will be his helpers toward God, and the disciples answer, we are God's helpers, we believe in God, bear witness that we have surrendered.
Christians, too, remember a small band of disciples who left their nets to follow Jesus. But what does it mean to help God, who needs nothing?

teach.h: HELP HIS CAUSE, AND HE HELPS YOU.
teach.b: Another verse says: if you help God, he will help you and make your feet firm. Commentators explain it as helping his cause: his religion and his messengers.
Some widen it to the people his law protects, the poor, the orphan, the wronged. The verse doesn't ask for heroes. It asks for the hand that goes up in the pause.

how: Muslims volunteer at mosques, charities and community kitchens, and speak of service to people in need as helping God's cause; Isa and his disciples are honored in the Qur'an.

o: helpers, the ones who answer when asked
the twelve disciples of Isa, by name
the emigrants who fled Mecca with nothing

games.q: helpers of God — tap the pairs.
p: who are my helpers for God?

s: the word ansar in the verse is the same word that named the Helpers of Medina
ansar means helpers, and later named the people of Medina.
commentators all agree on what hawariyyun means
some said whitening cloth, some purity of heart, some close supporters.
the same scene with Isa and the disciples appears in Surah Al 'Imran
there too the disciples answer, we are God's helpers.

games.q: Isa son of Maryam turns to his disciples and asks: who are my helpers for God? what do they say?
games.why: they answered, we are God's helpers, and the verse asks believers to answer the same way.

practice: Think of a place near you that runs on helpers: a mosque, a food bank, a shelter, a school, a neighbor who's struggling. Picture the moment someone asks, who'll help, and picture your hand going up.
Choose one concrete offer you could make: an hour, a skill, a donation, a lift.

wordCard.voice: Ansar: helpers, the word the disciples of Isa used for themselves, and the word Surah As-Saff asks believers to be. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: be helpers of God. ansar is the plural of nasir, helper.

carryVoice: Your line: be a helper. Teams start with one hand in the air. Day six hundred twenty-five.
